title: Palomino Insurance — cold→pilot outreach flow (working notes)
content:
Notes to self — quick TL;DR:

- Palomino Insurance is a mid-market P&C insurer with acquisitive product strategy (regional brokers + digital direct). Tech org moderate size (~40 eng), several legacy vendor contracts for claims triage/chatbot, reportedly evaluating upstream automation vendors.
- Why they matter: sizable claims volume (peak season claims spikes), sensitivity to per‑request cost for customer-facing chat, and strict data residency needs for certain lines. Likely receptive to Dedicated/Private options where we can promise predictable unit economics and data separation.

Account summary (public + hints):
- HQ: Denver, CO. ~1.2B revenue (2024 press release).
- Recent signals: job posting for "Head of AI Automation"; RFP posted on X for "claims AI" in Dec 2025 (source: vendor list).
- Existing stack: Zendesk for CX, in-house underwriting rules, AWS for core infra (VPC presence in us-west-2).

Key people (to confirm):
- Maria Gutierrez — Dir. of Claims Ops (likely primary for claims triage pilots)
  - Notes: quoted in 2025 webinar about improving TAT; reachable via LinkedIn.
- Anil Sharma — Head of Data Science / ML (decision influencer)
  - Notes: likely cares about model reproducibility, rollout controls, batch scoring for subrogation.
- CTO (unknown name) — procurement escalation; sets security/KMS decisions.

Primary value alignment (how Redwood helps):
- Cost predictability: Dedicated pools + batching guidance to bring down per‑token cost for high‑volume claim chat.
- Reliability/SLOs: fallbacks and regional routing to avoid downtime during peak claims season.
- Compliance/data residency: Redwood Private (VPC + KMS) for PHI-adjacent claimant data and audit logs.
- Ops/deploy velocity: model pinning + canary rollouts to reduce risk of regressions in responses that affect claims outcomes.

Objections we should prep for (notes + rebuttals):
1) "We already have a chatbot vendor / vendor lock-in."
   - Rebuttal: focus on interoperability — Redwood can sit behind existing chat UX as the LLM engine; start with a small routing percentage to avoid rip-and-replace. Highlight migration play: prefix caching to reduce upfront cost and maintain UX parity.
2) "Security & compliance concerns with hosted APIs."
   - Rebuttal: propose Private deployment (VPC) + HSM/KMS; offer SOC2 + sample audit artifact; draft an NDA-first pilot contract. Keiko to pull standard SCA.
3) "We don't trust LLM outputs for adjudication/claims decisions."
   - Rebuttal: propose bounded assist mode — LLM suggests candidate text, human signs off. Use Canary + rollback + evals tied to prompts; Redwood Optimize can monitor regressions vs golden prompt set.
4) "Cost — what if token bill spikes?"
   - Rebuttal: show historical batching + cache numbers from similar pilot (Samir's Retail case), propose hard caps and alerting, and offer predictable Dedicated pricing for pilot term.

Suggested outbound sequence (cold→pilot conversion) — 6-touch multichannel, timeboxed over 6 weeks:
- Touch 1 (Email day 0): short intro to Maria (claims ops). 2 paragraphs: who we are (redwood inference), one line on pilot idea (reduce claims TAT + preserve human oversight), ask for 20m call.
  Subject: "Pilot idea: reduce claims TAT without changing UX"
  CTA: two times for a 20m call + ask for correct contact if not Maria.
- Touch 2 (LinkedIn + connection note day 2): mention email, quick stat — "we cut average token cost by ~40% on batch-heavy workloads."
- Touch 3 (Email day 7): short one-pager PDF (attach) — list of guardrails, compliance options, intro to Private deployment.
- Touch 4 (Call + voicemail day 14): 2-line voicemail, follow-up Slack or email recap.
- Touch 5 (Email day 21): pilot proposal outline (6‑8 week pilot, success metrics, roles), include simple SOW bullets.
- Touch 6 (Exec intro / procurement loop day 30–40): if warmed, loop in CTO/procurement with security artifacts + contract template.

Cold email draft — version A (concise):
Hi Maria,

I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference — we help platform teams run high-throughput, predictable LLM inference with private deployment options. We recently ran a 6-week pilot with a mid-market insurer that reduced average claims triage time by ~18% while keeping humans in the loop for final decisions.

If reducing claims TAT while keeping your existing triage UX is interesting, could I book 20 minutes next week to sketch a low-risk pilot? Two times that work: Tue 3/10 10am MT or Wed 3/11 2pm MT.

— Jordan

Call script (20m):
- 0–3m intro, confirm pain: "how are claim volumes / peak load handled today?"
- 3–8m share outcomes from similar pilot (metrics + constraints)
- 8–13m map Redwood capabilities to their constraints (private deployment, SLOs, rollouts)
- 13–17m walk pilot plan (data needs, sample size, success criteria)
- 17–20m next steps + decision owner clarification

Pilot SOW (high level bullets):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2w setup & model onboarding, 3w live test, 1w analysis)
- Scope: integrate Redwood inference behind existing chat/claims UX; route X% traffic; human-in-the-loop for adjudication
- Success metrics: reduce TAT by >=12% OR reduce average agent touches by >=1 OR maintain NPS for claimant interactions
- Security: VPC deployment, KMS integration, audit logs retained 90 days

Data ask (minimum to get started):
- 1–2 weeks anonymized claim transcripts (prefer jsonl), traffic pattern (tokens/req distribution), and current latency targets.

Open questions / unknowns (research tasks):
- Confirm Maria's email + org chart for Claims Tech. (LinkedIn signals ambiguous)
- Which broker lines are most likely to run digital-first triage? auto vs homeowners? (ask in call)
- Internal procurement SLA thresholds for third-party infra — do they accept monthly reserved capacity?

To-dos (who/when):
- Keiko: pull SOC2 + sample audit doc, run legal quick-check on pilot NDA (due 2026-03-06).
- Samir: prepare 2‑page one-pager with metrics from Retail pilot (due 2026-02-05) — include batch/caching numbers.
- Jordan(me): warm intro to Maria via LinkedIn, send version A email, schedule follow-ups (target first outreach week of Feb).

Quick rebuttal snippets (for SDRs/on-call):
- "We can run behind your UI + route small % of live traffic — no disruption to agents."
- "Private deploy + KMS — we hand over logs and keys; you keep custody of sensitive data."
- "We only suggest candidate responses; humans approve final text for adjudication use cases."

Slack + comms notes:
- Initial convo to scout in #partner-scout; once Maria responds, move thread to #partner-engage and tag Keiko + Samir.
- If legal requests more docs: route to #legal-quick-help with JIRA-GTM-732.

Hypotheses to test during pilot (metrics we can instrument):
- Prefix caching hit rate — target >25% in week 2
- End-to-end latency p95 — keep <350ms for chat median path
- Human approval rate on suggested text — expected ~60% accept rate first month

Potential escalation / next-phase offers after pilot:
- Dedicated capacity + reserved commits for peak season (6–12 months)
- Move to private on-prem bundle if regulatory bar rises

Random notes / brain-dump (unfinished):
- Could propose a "claims playbook" template with golden prompts per claim type — Redwood Optimize + eval harness to lock regressions.
- If Palomino worried about vendor churn, propose a 3‑month rolling pilot with option to export model snapshots + prompt set.

End of doc. Keep short bullets in outreach copy; save deep technical artifacts for later, but have SOC2 + KMS screenshots ready.
